name: Question 14
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\sqrt{t}-{t}^{3/2}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{4}{15}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\sqrt{t}-{t}^{3/2})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5/2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{4}{15}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{15} & =\frac{2}{3}(1)^{3/2}-\frac{2}{5}(1)^{5/2}+C \\ \frac{4}{15} & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2}{5}+C \\ \frac{4}{15} & =\frac{4}{15}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5/2}.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5/2}=0 \\ \frac{2}{5}{t}^{3/2}(\frac{5}{3}-t) & =0 \\ t & =0,\,\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t>0$, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{5}{3}\,\text{s}.$

Question 14
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=t−t3/2, where t>0 is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=415m/s when t=1s, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

a
t=115s
b
t=53s
c
t=35s
d
t=13s
e
t=310s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The particle is stationary when v=0m/s.

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(t−t3/2)dt=23t3/2−25t5/2+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=415. Substituting this into the above gives 415=23(1)3/2−25(1)5/2+C415=23−25+C415=415+CC=0. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=23t3/2−25t5/2.

Now, we find the moments in time when v=0m/s:

23t3/2−25t5/2=025t3/2(53−t)=0t=0,53.

Since t>0, the particle is stationary when t=53s.
